snippets.output: Fatigue, dark urine, and conjunctival icterus suggest hemolytic anemia. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels are consistent with hemolysis. A hemoglobin level of 7.2 g/dL further supports the diagnosis of hemolytic anemia.
snippets.pattern_notes: Three parallel findings supporting the diagnosis of hemolytic anemia - enumeration of supporting evidence.

snippets.output: The direct bilirubin level is elevated, indicating that the jaundice is due to direct (conjugated) bilirubin, which is produced when hemoglobin is broken down.
snippets.pattern_notes: Causal chain: elevated direct bilirubin -> jaundice from conjugated bilirubin -> produced by hemoglobin breakdown.

snippets.output: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole can cause hemolysis in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.
